statement: A large square is divided into two smaller squares and three rectangles. Each small square has area $a$, each rectangle has area $b$. If $a + b = 24$ and $\sqrt{a}$ is a natural number, find all possible areas of the large square.
A sequence satisfies $a_{n+1} = a_n + \frac{1}{a_n}$. Prove that for any positive real $a_0$, we have $a_{1996} > 63$.

A store sells bottles of 1 to 1996 liters. Two bottles have the same price iff their capacities $m, n$ (with $m > n$) satisfy $m - n = 1000$; a bottle of $m$ liters ($1 \leq m \leq 1000$) costs $1996 - m$ dollars. Find all pairs with $m + n = 1996$ of minimal total cost from which any integer $k \in [1, 1996]$ liters can be measured.

Start with the sequence $0, \underbrace{1, 1, \ldots, 1}_{1995}$. Repeatedly select some numbers (not all) and replace one of them by the arithmetic mean of the chosen ones. Prove all 1996 numbers can be made equal.

Completely cover a $k \times k$ square ($k > 1$ integer) using $1$ rectangle of size $1\times1$, $2$ of size $2\times1$, $4$ of size $3\times1$, $\ldots$, $2^n$ of size $(n+1)\times1$, without overlapping or extending beyond. Find all valid $k$.

Find all integers $n \geq 3$ for which there exists a set $S_n$ of $n$ points in the plane such that: no three are collinear, and no point lies inside the circle with diameter determined by any two points of $S_n$.
